reference.method: mpmath at 50 significant digits from the Double inputs; survival values summed or integrated on their own side

cases.name: Loan defaults, Binomial
cases.purpose: The default example: 100 independent loans, each defaulting with probability 2%.

cases.name: Loan defaults, Poisson
cases.purpose: The same portfolio as a Poisson count: 0.02 defaults per loan-year over 100 loan-years.

cases.name: Fair coin
cases.purpose: A symmetric Binomial: the median is the quantile of 0.5.

cases.name: Step boundary
cases.purpose: q = 0.74 lies just below the step F(1) = 0.75: F(0) = 0.25 < q <= F(1), so the quantile is 1 and F(Q) is above q. A q exactly on the step would leave the answer to the last bit of the computed tail.

cases.name: Threshold zero
cases.purpose: k = 0: fewer than 0 is impossible and at least 0 is certain; F(0) = exp(-3) is just below q.

cases.name: Threshold at n
cases.purpose: k = n: at most n is certain and more than n impossible.

cases.name: Large mean
cases.purpose: A Poisson mean of 500: the window is about 220 counts wide.

cases.name: Rare events
cases.purpose: 5000 trials with p = 0.001: the Binomial is close to a Poisson of mean 5.

cases.name: Far quantile
cases.purpose: A mean of 0.5 and q = 0.999999: the quantile lies beyond mean + 5 standard deviations.
